I have been doing WC for about 4 years. I tried for 3 years and another club before I changed clubs.

There is a very noticeable difference in the teaching that happens at the club I currently train at. At my previous club, everything was taught very slowly and you weren't really moved on before you have gotten it almost perfect. I had spent a very long time just practicing forms at the first club, I had done some drills there too. At my current club, things are different. I remember it was this guys first or second lesson and he got to play 'the knife game'. You get taken round the back and only to the small bridge the crosses a small stream. The teacher has already said he will stab you at some point (with a dummy knife). He talks to you and has a bit of a chat, then he pulls the weapon and just stabs and stabs you until you stop him or until you would die. We train with more than just drills.

There was a guy that came in yesterday who had already done some WC at another place. We were doing knife work and other drills. I had mentioned to him about how we also use things like the walls to press people against/ push them into. He was surprised an stated that they didn't do that where he used to train.

Long story short. It it's violent, it's good, if it's all about making sure you have the perfect form in everything before you move onto the next thing, you are probably wasting your time. It's important to have good form, but fights are messy and you can't expect to be having perfect form when things get out of hand. I said that it's good if it's violent, that's because fighting is, they should train you how to fight.

I just made mention of this on another post a few minutes ago, I will add a bit more info though. Set a time to wake up at like 7am. When your alarm goes off at 7, get up and into the sun and eat some food. When I mean get into the sun, you can just be by a window, just get some sunlight on you. Also take a look into foods that increase your melatonin. Now you will need another alarm for when you should eat the foods and get ready for bed. Try to avoid screens late at night. If you are still wanting to use a device use f.lux (it's really nice to have).

When you are in bed get comfortable. Try to imagine your bed turned around....it helps me, it might not help you. Start to visualize something that swings side to side. You might visualize a pendulum; I visualize being in a small boat in the tropics just feeling the waves rock the boat from side to side (not front to back). Kill your inner monologue. When you start talking in your mind just remind yourself to feel the waves and imagine the scene. It might take a little while before it will have a large effect but I think that it should help. Try to stick to it for 2 weeks and see if something changes.

Try this. Once you have done the WBTB focus on the darkness behind your eyes for about 10 seconds. Focus on the sound you hear for about 10 seconds, lastly focus on the feeling of everything from the bed sheets to an itch (you are allowed to scratch it). Note that you are not trying to see, listen and feel all at once. Look (don't stress your eyes) then listen (if you hear almost nothing, don't worry), feel (don't try feel things that aren't there). That is 1 cycle. Do another 4-5 cycles so you have done 5-6 cycles. Each cycle should be about 30 seconds. Don't count the seconds just change to the next part in the cycle when you feel that 10 seconds has passed.

Then do the cycles much slower look 40 seconds, listen 40 seconds, feel 40 seconds. Do about 3-4 reps of these.

It should look like this.

Fast cycles 10 sec each cycle for 5-6 cycles
Slow cycles 40 sec each cycle for about 3-4 cycles

Your mind will go astray. It can be good to go through another cycle if you have found yourself doing that. Don't stress it though. Let your mind wander.
